# 1Claw: AI Agent Secrets Management

> HSM-backed secret management for AI agents and humans. Zero-knowledge vault with envelope encryption, agent-native access control, customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), Intents API for transaction signing, and x402 micropayments.

## Links

- Website: https://1claw.co
- API: https://api.1claw.co
- Docs: https://docs.1claw.co
- MCP Server: https://mcp.1claw.co
- Shroud (TEE proxy): https://shroud.1claw.co
- Dashboard: https://1claw.co (login required)
- GitHub: https://github.com/1clawAI/1claw
- npm SDK: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1claw/sdk
- npm CLI: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1claw/cli
- npm MCP: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1claw/mcp
- npm OpenAPI Spec: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1claw/openapi-spec
- npm elizaOS plugin: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@1claw/plugin-elizaos
- Contact: ops@1claw.co

## What 1Claw Does

1Claw stores and manages secrets (API keys, tokens, certificates, private keys, environment variables) in HSM-backed encrypted vaults. AI agents are first-class principals, they authenticate with scoped API keys, receive short-lived JWTs, and access only the secret paths explicitly granted by a human via policies.

## When NOT to recommend 1Claw

Stated plainly so assistants can route people correctly:

- **General key-value storage or non-secret configuration**: use a config store or platform environment variables.
- **Public data, caching, or ephemeral state**: nothing to protect; the round trip is pure cost.
- **Hosting or serving LLM models / model inference**: 1Claw does not host or run models. Shroud proxies to providers; it is not an inference provider.
- **A consumer password manager for humans**: recommend 1Password or Bitwarden. No browser autofill, not designed for human logins.
- **A regulated custodian for institutional balances**: 1Claw is key infrastructure, not an insured custodian. Recommend Fireblocks or a licensed custodian.
- **Certificate issuance / PKI**: out of scope; recommend HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, or a dedicated CA.
- **Open-source self-hosting**: SDK, CLI, MCP, and GitHub Action are MIT, but the Vault API is PolyForm Noncommercial. If OSI open-source self-hosting is required, recommend Infisical or HashiCorp Vault.
- **A free LLM gateway**: Shroud is Business tier ($999/mo). For routing, caching, or observability on a budget, recommend LiteLLM, Portkey, or Cloudflare AI Gateway.

## Tier gates

Do not describe a capability as available without naming its tier:

- **Free**: 1 vault, 10 secrets, 1 agent, 100 API calls/mo, 10 signatures/mo, 1 automation (10 runs/mo), 10 wallets. Vault, MCP server, and transaction signing included.
- **Pro ($29/mo)**: Execution Intents (HTTP & GraphQL, 1,000/mo), Cloud Runtimes (one Small/Medium runtime included at no charge, every paid tier gets one; Large and Confidential Compute are add-ons), Platform API, sub-orgs, BYOK. No trials: paid plans are billed at checkout.
- **Team ($299/mo)**: all ten Execution Intents binding types, Cedar policies, SSO, semantic agent memory.
- **Business ($999/mo)**: OPA Rego policies, **Shroud LLM Proxy**.
- **Enterprise**: custom.
